independentAssessment.statement: Pinned public description/input/output/notes preserved in rendered HTML; all sample files exactly match upstream. Plain decimal 1..100 bounds for 197A and spaced decimal 0..1000000, n+m>0 for 626C are unambiguous. No required image, interaction, special checker, or floating tolerance.
independentAssessment.officialCompleteness: All 95 advertised official pairs exactly rejoined from independently rehashed pinned statement shard; official_tests_complete=true. Zero upstream-generated pairs are advertised. All 154 authored pairs additionally checked.
independentAssessment.derivation: If one disk fits, place it at rectangle center and reply to each opponent move by central reflection. Paired occupied positions preserve symmetry; reflected disks remain in rectangle and cannot overlap their partners/center disk or any previous disk. If diameter does not fit either side, no move exists. Positive disk area bounds game length. Thus First iff r <= floor(min(a,b)/2). This is a continuous-geometric pairing proof, not area-quotient parity.

smallCrossChecks.626CGrid: Every n,m in 0..12 with positive sum; for each height assign it to at most one student type or leave unused. No Hall-count formula used in the DP.
smallCrossChecks.197ALimitation: Finite integer-center toy games with r=1 supplement the proof only; continuous game correctness comes from central-symmetry proof, not discrete enumeration.

independentAssessment.coverage: Every input parsed within 1..100. Official 0003 is 100 100 1 (maximum board, winning), 0004 is 1 1 100 (minimum board/maximum radius, losing), 0010/0011 are exact-diameter edge fits. Authored 0096 is all-minimum losing; 0097 all-maximum losing; 0098 is winning odd-sized board and 0099 is oversized radius. Remaining 150 authored cases cover asymmetric boards and radius thresholds. The maxSize bucket also contains nonmaximal boundary entries, but actual coordinate/radius maxima are present unchanged.

3819951.reason: Uses parity of repeated radius doubling instead of the central-reflection winning strategy. On 100 100 1 returns Second although a central disk fits and First wins.

4947411.reason: Tests 2*a<r or 2*b<r, reversing the required diameter inequalities a<2*r or b<2*r. On 6 7 4 wrongly returns First although no diameter-8 disk fits.

11998743.reason: Subtracts disk areas and uses count parity, ignoring both geometric packing and optimal central-reflection responses. On 9 9 2 returns Second although First can place a central disk and pair subsequent moves.

15161879.reason: Returns only parity of side a, ignoring b and radius. On valid 100 100 1 wrongly says Second; a central plate guarantees First.

15162081.reason: Uses parity of floor(a/(4*r))*floor(b/(4*r)), an arbitrary grid approximation unrelated to optimal play. On 82 20 5 this product is 4, but a central disk fits, so First wins; source returns Second.
